units.title: Comparing notes on the stairwell (please add yours)
units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, as Bev suggested, I am starting a page where we each write down plainly what we have noticed, so that the meeting tomorrow has something to read. Mine: the lights between 6 and 8 have been out every night since day 1. Coming down from 8 at about half past six in the morning, I hear steps behind me which stop when I stop. I do not think it is a person. Irena, 7C

units.title: Lift out again (third time this week)
units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Lift out again since last night. The engineer's sticker says 'next visit day 9'. I have a hip, a shopping trolley and three flights, and I am not one of the upper-floor people who can afford to be frightened of stairs. Somebody at Kerrow should try carrying a week of tins up from the shop and then write me a notice about patience.

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Nothing happens below 6, I can tell you that for nothing, and I would wager nothing happens above it either. It is the lights, it is the lift, and it is people frightening each other in the dark. While you are writing things down, write down that the bins on 3 have not been emptied since day 4.

units.author: dc_12_ollie
units.text: my mum says write that the year 9s at school say dellow court has a man on the stairs who counts. i dont know what he counts. somebody in my class asked me if its true because i live here and i said probably not. is it true

units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: Mine, for the list. R. still says 'the man on the stairs waits for us'. Today he said the man waits on 7, and that he is polite. I am fairly sure he got it from the same year 9s Ollie mentions, through his cousin. I don't use the stairs with the kids now, only the lift, and only when it works. Soraya, 11F

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Thank you all, this is exactly what I wanted for tomorrow. The meeting is at 19:00 in the community room on the ground floor. The kettle will be on and Hassan has promised biscuits. Please keep notes factual, and please don't name neighbours who haven't posted themselves. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: For the list. Day 5, 23:10, I came down from 8 to 6 after my route. I recorded on my phone. The steps continue after I stop. There isn't a fridge on that floor. It is the bin store. I wrote this also on LowBand where they are analysing it. Sorry for my spelling.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Not a resident, but Benedikt invited me over. For the list: the recording has a 58 Hz compressor hum underneath it, cycling. Something on or near that riser is running a compressor. That is not a dismissal, it is a lead. Find the compressor and you may find the steps, or at least what is shaking the concrete.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: lads it's the wind. tower blocks whistle and creak. my brother lived in one in weyhaven for six years and in a westerly it sounded like a choir practising. nobody wrote a list about it.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Mr Pryce, I can bring your shopping to the door until the lift is fixed, no charge. Just leave a list in the shop. Same for anyone above 5 who needs it. Bread was three hours late this morning because of the fog, sorry to everyone who came down early. I have wind-up torches at cost, 4 dollars. H

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: ok not joking for once. came back about 1am, lift dead again, took the stairs up from the ground. lights out from 6. went up 6 to 7 on my phone torch and the steps above me kept going a bit after i stopped on the landing. four or five. then nothing. i stood there like an idiot for a minute. probably echo off the well. i'm writing it because irena asked for notes, not because i'm scared. (a bit)

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: Added a sketch for the list (pencil, phone photo, terrible light): the riser from my landing on 14, looking down the well. The lit floors show as rings and the dark band between 6 and 8 is a missing tooth. For the record, some nights I hear steps go up past 14, where there is only the roof door. I have decided they are the caretaker (I have never met the caretaker).

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: morning all, home from the depot at five like always and walked up to 5 the way I always do and never heard a thing love, not a single step, which is either good news or very bad news and I can't decide which, anyway I've read Jordie's and I've put the kettle on and Jordie if you want a brew before bed knock on 5D

units.title: Dellow stairwell recording: quick analysis
units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Quick analysis of Benedikt's stairwell file, the phone recording cross-posted yesterday. There is a steady tone at 58 Hz with harmonics at 116 and 174, on for about 40 s and off for about 15. That is a refrigeration compressor signature. The footsteps sit on top of it and are broadband, which fits structure-borne impact in a concrete riser. Nothing here needs more than a fridge and a resident.

units.title: Fog walk, Weyhaven dock road (binaural)
units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on for this one. A 25-minute binaural walk along the Weyhaven dock road in thick fog last night. Fog really does eat the top end: gulls overhead sound like they are behind a curtain, and footsteps across the road arrive soft and late. The ships' generators are the loudest thing, a low wall in front and to the left the whole way.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Fog does odd things over water too. Still air plus a temperature inversion and sound bends back down instead of escaping upward. On nights like this I have heard a winch on Lisle from Gilliver harbour, nine kilometres. Lovely file. Nice generator, sounds like a two-stroke auxiliary.

units.title: Brackwater knocks and the reservoir valve works
units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Possibly relevant to dunlin's knocks: the council has posted outflow valve maintenance at Brackwater reservoir for three nights from tonight, 22:00 to 05:00, with a note that residents may hear knocking in pipes. Water hammer in a long outflow main can travel a long way and come up out of the ground as discrete thumps. Worth logging which of tonight's events line up with the works.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Thank you for the analysis. But there isn't a fridge on that floor. Floor 8 at the stairwell end is the bin store. Bins, a mop sink, a light that is broken. No fridge. I go past it every night after my route, sometimes twice when I forget the post.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on for this one, everyone. Whatever the hum is, the steps place above and behind the mic, and the last few move closer while Benedikt is standing still. A fridge doesn't walk down a stair. Hollis, I would love you to listen on decent cans rather than monitors before deciding.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: That's a pump. Or a valve actuator. Ninety percent of knocks near water are pumps and the other ten are hulls. Ask the water office for the pump log, not the works notice. They will have one going back years, even for the old pumping house.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: I did listen on cans. A phone mic in a concrete stairwell gets reflections off every landing, so 'above and behind' can just as easily be the wall above and behind. Localisation in a riser is not reliable. And Benedikt, compressors are not only in fridges: vending units, chillers, dehumidifiers, a chest freezer in a flat. The 58 Hz is real.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Thanks, that is a fair thing to log and I will keep a column for it. The works only start tonight, though. My first knocks were on day 2, and there were no works that night that I know of. I've emailed the water office to ask whether anything was running then. Make of it what you will.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Mod note: thanks all, this is a good thread. Benedikt, if you still have it, please post the raw file from the phone rather than the copy you shared through the chat app, which has been compressed and smeared. And let's keep it to what is on the recording. LowBand is for recordings, not stories.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so the old pumping house on the reservoir road has been derelict since the 90s, I walk past it every week, the doors are chained and there's a birch growing through the roof. no pumps in there at all. the outflow main does run right past it though so Hollis's thing could still work?? sorry, I mean it could still work, one question mark

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Benedikt, please send me the raw file as well. I would like to time the individual impacts. 1. Two flights at 19 per flight is 38 steps if taken singly. 2. I will mark onsets on a clean waveform. 3. I will post the count and the method. No conclusions until n is known.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: guys this is insane, knocks in the woods AND an abandoned pumping house?? im coming down there this week with full kit, thermal cam, spirit box, the lot. stream link in bio. dunlin can i use your clips for the trailer, ill credit you

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: I will post the raw file tomorrow, it is on my old phone which is in the van. Sorry for the compressed one. Again, I checked the bin store tonight on my way up. No fridge. A dead mop and many bags. The light in there still does not work.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: nightscream, please ask permission by private message, not in a thread, and expect most people here to say no if music is going on top. Also, the woods are private estate land after dusk and the keeper has already asked people to stay out. Recordings, not stories.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: No, please don't use them, thanks. Back from the footpath: nothing tonight between 23:00 and 02:30 except a tawny pair and a lot of drip off the trees. The valve works were audible as a low hiss near the dam at 23:40, nothing like a knock. Logged it anyway. Going to bed.

units.title: Corridor lights switch on for someone who never arrives
units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: thesis log, night 41: the corridor outside my lab has motion-sensor lights. Tonight at 01:10 they came on at the far end, then the next panel, then the next, like someone walking toward my door at a normal pace. Nobody arrived. The lights timed out after two minutes. I am on my fourth energy drink, so feel free to discount me entirely.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: same campus? the sensors on the science block are older than you. my cousin did facilities there. they trigger on warm air from the heating vents. also come and buy something that isn't an energy drink. we have bananas. they are yellow.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: the heating goes off at midnight to save money (we are all very cold, I have a hat on indoors) so it isn't warm air, unless it is the ghost of warm air. bananas noted. I will buy one banana as a gesture of good faith and eat it at my desk like a professional.

units.title: Housekeeping, start of the week
units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: a reminder that Lamp Hours is for company on the night shift, not campfire stories. Odd things at work are fine to share; please say what you saw, when, and what you checked. Please don't post screenshots from other forums. And drink some water, all of you. Ines (mod)

units.title: Gate 7 camera log
units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Log, gate 7. 00:48 monitor 6 shows a figure standing at the NE edge of the lot where the floodlight ends. Static, about a minute. Radioed, walked it, on site 00:53. Patrolled, nil found. No footprints in the wet. Monitor 6 clear on return. Third time this week, same corner. Logged for IT.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Does monitor 6 go through the same recorder as the others? Ghost images from a slow sensor in low light are common, particularly where something passed earlier. Ask IT whether that camera has a night persistence or noise-reduction setting. It is a lens-and-software problem far more often than it is anything in the lot.

units.title: The van outside the bakery, again
units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: That white van was back outside the bakery tonight, engine running from about 01:30. No light in the cab, just exhaust curling up in the street lamp like steam off a proving drawer. Still there when the first loaves came out at 02:40. Nobody got out to buy one, which frankly is the strangest part.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Will ask. IT only come in on day shift, so it may be a few days. Noted your settings question in the book under monitor 6. Back on patrol.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: I will walk past it when I bring the rolls round at 4. If it is the same plates as last time I will note them. Patrolled the yard at 03:00, nil found, as ever.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Two things to check before anything else. Are the panels on a shared circuit, so one trigger cascades down the run? And how long had you been awake? A cascading sensor fault plus a twenty-hour day makes a very convincing person. n of 1, but I have watched our own clinic corridor do exactly this.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Water drunk, Ines. Also tea. Also a hot chocolate from the B corridor machine, which tonight gave me the chocolate first and the cup second. Mopped. Small victories on the night run.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Had the same at the retail park earlier this week. Four hours idling at the edge of the car park lights. Control said 'sleeping driver'. I walked up with a torch and the cab was empty, engine running, keys in. Nobody came back while I was on shift. Still bugs me, if I'm honest.

units.title: 03:10 again
units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: It buzzed again at 03:10. I was sitting with Mrs A. in the lounge because she could not settle, and when the front door intercom went she patted my hand and said 'that's for me, love', the same as every night. I went to the door. There is never anyone. I check the screen and the step. I am writing this so I stop thinking about it.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: A lot of vans have a sleeping bunk behind the seats with a curtain across. From outside: empty cab. Behind the curtain: a very tired man with the heater on and his boots off. I would bet on that before anything else, Dev.

units.title: B corridor vending report
units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Vending report, B corridor, Port Ammet General. Machine 2 now offers 'soup (tomato)' and 'soup (tomato)' as separate buttons. I pressed both. They are different soups. One of them is not tomato. The porters' lodge is divided. Quiet night otherwise, which I am not allowed to say out loud.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Ours on the ward does something like it, a name instead of a buzz. Estates think it is the call button. Yours sounds like a wiring fault to me, damp gets into outdoor units this time of year. Be kind to yourself, it's a long shift and she's lucky to have you. Back to it.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Never say quiet, you will get a run of admissions. Ours only has the one soup and it has been 'out of order' since the spring, with a handwritten sign that someone has corrected twice. I am jealous of your mystery soup. Back to it.

units.title: Fare of the night
units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: fare of the night was a man in a full wedding suit, no wedding, said he went to the wrong church and stayed anyway because the cake looked good and nobody asked, tipped me in coins he said were from the collection plate, I didn't ask anyway the rank is quiet now and the fog has lifted off the river

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Fair, I didn't check behind the seats. Nobody answered the window knock though, and I knocked hard enough to hurt my knuckle. Maybe he was very, very tired. Control has started calling it 'Dev's van', which doesn't help.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: I would read that novel. I suspect I have already read that novel and sold it twice. Glad the fog has lifted somewhere; it is still sitting on Tollinby like damp wool, and the shop smells of it.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Walked past at 04:05. Same van, engine off now, dew on the windscreen, so it had been off a while. Plates noted, same as last week. No one inside that I could see, curtain or not. Took the rolls in. They were very good.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Liv is on the bus home now. Damp in the junction box, that is my bet too. Same thing on the shaft-top intercom every winter, it buzzes on its own when the rain gets in. I will look at it on my day off if the home lets me.

units.title: End of shift
units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: End of shift. On the bus. Pump on level 4 died at 02:00, so we carried it up in pieces. Cap lamps all fine. The new lad asked why the old men stand close in the lamp when they talk on the level. Told him it is manners. He wrote it down. He writes everything down.

units.title: Back corridor update
units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Corridor update for those who asked. Night five: Biscuit (old beagle cross) walked the front run fine, then sat at the back corridor door at 02:10 and would not budge, lead or treat. Juno did the same at 02:25. I walked it alone with the torch. Nothing on the floor, nothing in the cages, a smell like warm dust. Wrote it in the book.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Warm dust could be a heater element or a fan motor running hot up in the ceiling. Dogs hear a bearing going long before we do. Get your maintenance fella to pop a tile. Meantime drink your coffee, stretch them legs, and don't walk that corridor tired, Jo.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Good thought, Merle. There is a vent right above that door. I'll ask Pete to look when he's in. Biscuit says thank you, he is currently asleep on my coat, which is not where his bed is.

units.title: Fog on the far coast
units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: A night of the slow kind. The beam goes out and comes back with nothing on it, sea fog lying in banks a mile offshore and the stars sharp above it, and I have spent an hour polishing brass that did not need it. There is a particular silence when the foghorn on the next headland stops. You hear the sea again, louder than you remembered it.

units.title: Depot lights (or not)
units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: evening all or morning I suppose, home from the depot, they still haven't fixed the wash bay lamps love so we did the 14s by torch again and the supervisor came round with his clipboard saying we'd missed the back seats, well yes, we can't see the back seats, anyway kettle on and then bed
